text:
anya: just kicked off a canary for flux11b-int4 (quantized from fp16) on dedicated staging. seeing intermittent OOMs around p95 for long-gen workloads (~512 max_new_tokens). logs attached below.

matt: can you paste the exact runtime config? batch size / max_new_tokens / prefetch?

anya: default route config, nothing special — batching=auto, max_new_tokens=512, prefetch=enabled, kv_cache_retention=default. we only changed quantization to int4 and swapped kernels.

liam: hmm int4 should be fine but fragmentation + kv cache growth at long seqs is a common pattern. curious if this is coldstart-only or sustained.

anya: seeing OOMs both on coldstart and after ~30s of steady traffic. p95 memory climbs then a sudden cuda OOM in the runtime. stack trace snippet: ```RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Attempted to allocate 1.2 GiB (GPU 0; 40.00 GiB total, 34.10 GiB free)```

ciara: can you check kv cache size per request? maybe kv isn't being trimmed for shorter turns. also what is batch packing doing — small requests could inflate peak.

anya: good call — sampling traces show large prefixes retained for ~20% of requests. batching seems to pack two long requests together occasionally, producing a big combined allocation.

matt: quick mitigation: set max_batch_size=1 for the canary route and set max_new_tokens_default=256 temporarily. and enable kv_trim_on_eviction=true. also add a small session cache TTL to drop stale prefixes.

liam: +1. also try disabling aggressive prefetch (set prefetch=off) — prefetch can pre-alloc extra workspace for kernels on int4 paths.

anya: rolling those now. config diff I pushed to the canary route: ```
route:
  batching:
    mode: manual
    max_batch_size: 1
  generation:
    default_max_new_tokens: 256
  kv_cache:
    trim_on_eviction: true
  prefetch: false
```

deploy-bot: deploy started for flux11b-int4 canary @anya (build 2026.03.21-5).

anya: after change, p95 mem usage dropped ~18% in first 10 minutes. no new OOMs so far in the small sample. baseline latency up slightly but still within SLO.

ciara: nice. we should run a focused perf test: 1) high-concurrency short requests, 2) low-concurrency long requests, 3) mixed. capture kv size distributions + peak allocs.

matt: Agreed. I can run a sweep tomorrow with the profiling hooks (alloc trace + nvprof). also want to test a lighter quant profile (int4 with 8-bit KV) — sometimes using 8-bit kv for cache + int4 weights reduces fragmentation.

liam: FYI add a regression eval set for quality — quant change might shift tokenization probabilities at long tails. run rollout check against our LLM-evals prompt set.

anya: added eval job to the canary pipeline. also flagged for follow-up: consider batching window limits (max_new_tokens-aware packing) so we don't co-pack two long max_new requests.

ciara: can we implement pack-aware gating? e.g. if request.max_new_tokens > 256, set pack_priority=low so it doesn't get batched with other large ones.

matt: that's a good policy. also record annotations on traces so we can retroactively find which requests were co-packed.

anya: thanks all — will monitor 2h then propose defaults for prod: default_max_new_tokens=256, batching=auto but max_batch_size=2 and pack-aware gating for >256. will open a follow-up thread with perf numbers. :thumbsup:
